cards.explanation: The answer is that David asks God to hide him from their scheming. He prays, "Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity…" (Psalm 64:2). He doesn't open with a battle plan. He runs to God first, friends. I think that's a pretty good place to start on a rough day.

The answer is tongues, friends! David says they "…sharpen their tongues like swords…" (Psalm 64:3). The sword is the comparison, and the tongue is what's being sharpened. Words can cut deep, and David knows it.

The answer is suddenly and without fear, friends. David says they are "…ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear." (Psalm 64:4). No warning and no worry on their side. That's what makes the ambush so sneaky.

The question they ask is "Who will see them?" friends. The verse says they speak of hiding their snares, and then the wicked say, "Who will see them?" (Psalm 64:5). That's the question they ask about their snares. I think they're hoping nobody does.
The answer is True, friends. The wicked say, "We have perfected a secret plan." (Psalm 64:6). Perfected! They think there are no loose ends. I've said that about a batch before it hit the floor.

The answer is False, friends. David doesn't say he'll fight back himself. Look at how the turn goes: "But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded." (Psalm 64:7). David isn't grabbing a weapon. He hands the whole thing to God, and I think that's a relief.

The answer is arrows, friends! David says, "But God will shoot them with arrows…" (Psalm 64:7). Remember how David said the mob aims their bitter words like arrows? Now God is the one who shoots. The verse goes on, "suddenly they will be wounded." (Psalm 64:7).

The answer is that their tongues will be turned against them, friends. David says, "They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them." (Psalm 64:8). Earlier in the psalm, those tongues were sharpened like swords. Now those same tongues are turned against them.

The answer is that all mankind will fear and proclaim God's work, friends. "Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God…" (Psalm 64:9). People see what God has done, and they can't keep quiet about it. They're talking about Him.

The answer is that the righteous rejoice and take refuge in the LORD, friends. "Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him…" (Psalm 64:10). David began by asking God to hide him, and he finishes by saying the righteous can run to God and be glad. It's a full circle.
